newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea warns of "serious consequences" over sub.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea warns of "serious consequences" over sub.

text.p: North Korea threatened "serious consequences" on Wednesday over the deaths of its soldiers who came ashore in South Korea from a submarine two weeks ago.
The threat came from Pyongyang military officers at a border meeting with the U.S.-led United Nations Command, which monitors a ceasefire that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
Of an estimated 26 North Koreans who landed on an east coast beach, 22 have been shot and killed by southern troops or found dead. One has been captured alive.

Korean People's Army officers repeated Pyongyang's earlier demand for the return of the submarine and the crew during the meeting in the border crossing village of Panmunjom, which North Korea requested.

"At the end of the meeting, the senior representative of the KPA delegation indicated that serious consequences, which would be announced, would occur as a result of the deaths of their soldiers," a U.N. Command statement said.
North Korea representatives again asserted the submarine accidentally drifted in to South Korean waters.
"The United Nations Command refuted the claim citing the considerable body of evidence the inflitration was a serious and deliberate violation of the Korean Armistice Agreement," the statement said.
It added that the U.N. Command protested against the threats, "pointing out that such threats make resolution of the situation more difficult".
North Korea has previously threatened to retaliate "a hundredfold or a thousandfold" over the incident, without being specific.
North Korean rhetoric against its arch-foe to the South is often exaggerated and violent.
However, South Korea has put its foreign diplomatic missions on extra alert following the latest threats. It is also beefing up its military forces to defend against any Pyongyang military action.
